title: Once you've fixed the bug that sent messages to the Dead Letter Queue, how do you reprocess them — the "redrive" flow of moving messages from the DLQ back to the main topic/queue so consumers retry them — and how do you do it safely (inspect/replay/discard tooling, idempotent consumers so replays don't cause duplicate side-effects, avoiding re-poisoning the main topic)?
shortTitle: Reprocessing dead letter queue messages safely (the redrive flow)

s1_definition.profdef: Redrive is the controlled process of moving records out of a dead letter queue back into the main topic or a reprocessing topic so that consumers, now running the fixed code, can handle them successfully. Doing it safely requires tooling to inspect, selectively replay, or discard records, idempotent consumers so that replayed records do not cause duplicate side effects, and guardrails so that still-poisonous records are not blindly pushed back and re-poison the main topic. Redrive is a deliberate operator action, not an automatic loop.
s1_definition.analogy: The dead letter queue is National Bank of India's problem tray full of transfer forms that failed. Once the bug that broke them is fixed, redrive is the supervisor carefully taking forms out of the problem tray and putting them back in the normal processing line. Safe redrive means the supervisor first reads each form to confirm it is now processable (inspect), only puts back the ones that should go (replay) and bins the ones that are genuinely junk (discard), and the clerks downstream are smart enough to notice "I already processed this exact form" so nobody is charged twice (idempotent consumers). The supervisor never dumps the whole tray back blindly, because that would just jam the line again.
s1_definition.oneliner: Redrive moves dead letter records back to the main flow under operator control, and it is safe only when consumers are idempotent and you inspect, selectively replay, or discard rather than blindly pushing everything back.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Redrive is the controlled process of moving records out of a dead letter queue back into the main topic or a reprocessing topic so that consumers, now running the fixed code, can handle them successfully. Doing it safely requires tooling to inspect, selectively replay, or discard records, idempotent consumers so that replayed records do not cause duplicate side effects, and guardrails so that still-poisonous records are not blindly pushed back and re-poison the main topic. Redrive is a deliberate operator action, not an automatic loop.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The dead letter queue is National Bank of India's problem tray full of transfer forms that failed. Once the bug that broke them is fixed, redrive is the supervisor carefully taking forms out of the problem tray and putting them back in the normal processing line. Safe redrive means the supervisor first reads each form to confirm it is now processable (inspect), only puts back the ones that should go (replay) and bins the ones that are genuinely junk (discard), and the clerks downstream are smart enough to notice "I already processed this exact form" so nobody is charged twice (idempotent consumers). The supervisor never dumps the whole tray back blindly, because that would just jam the line again.

**One line to remember:** Redrive moves dead letter records back to the main flow under operator control, and it is safe only when consumers are idempotent and you inspect, selectively replay, or discard rather than blindly pushing everything back.

sections.s2_technical:
Redrive begins only after the root cause is fixed. If you replay records before fixing the bug that sent them to the dead letter queue, they fail again and you are back where you started, so the precondition is a deployed fix. The dead letter records should carry metadata that you captured when they failed, such as the original topic, partition, offset, exception, and a correlation id, which is what makes inspection and targeted replay possible.

The first capability is inspection. You read the dead letter topic without committing destructive changes and examine each record and its error header to decide what it is: a transient failure that the fix now resolves, a permanent failure that should be discarded or corrected, or something needing manual handling. A good redrive tool lets you filter, for example by error type or time window, so you replay only the relevant subset.

The second capability is selective replay. For records that should be reprocessed, you publish them back, either to the original main topic or, more safely, to a dedicated reprocessing topic that the same consumer logic also reads. Publishing to a separate reprocessing topic avoids mixing replayed traffic with live traffic and lets you throttle it. You preserve the original key so partitioning and ordering semantics are respected. You throttle the replay rate so a large backlog does not overwhelm the consumers or downstream dependencies.

The third capability is discard. Some dead letter records are genuinely unprocessable, like a malformed record from a bug that should never have existed, and the correct action is to discard them, with an audit trail, rather than replay them.

The safety pillar is idempotent consumers. Because a record may have partially processed before failing, or may be replayed more than once, the consumer must produce the same result whether it sees a record once or many times. You achieve this by keying side effects on a business id, for example recording that transfer TRD-001 was already applied and skipping it if seen again, or using an upsert keyed on the id. Without idempotency, redrive risks double debits, double fees, or double settlements, which in a bank is unacceptable.

The anti-pattern to avoid is re-poisoning. If you blindly loop the entire dead letter queue back into the main topic, any record that is still poisonous, because it was permanent, not transient, immediately fails again and may stall or flood the pipeline. So redrive is gated by classification and inspection, never an automatic unconditional loop. The senior nuances are that redrive should be an explicit, audited, rate-limited operator action, that you should track how many records were replayed, succeeded, and re-failed, and that a healthy practice is a reprocessing topic plus idempotent consumers plus a dashboard, so redrive is observable and reversible.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — A bug in National Bank of India's settlement consumer rejected valid transfers with amounts above a threshold, sending them to transfers.DLT. The team fixed the bug and now needs to reprocess the quarantined transfers. This is exactly the redrive scenario: move the dead letter records back for the fixed consumer to handle.

Problem 2 — Some dead letter records are genuinely malformed and must not be replayed, and some valid ones were already partially applied before failing. Replaying blindly could double-apply a transfer. This is exactly why redrive needs inspection, selective replay versus discard, and idempotent consumers.

We simulate the redrive flow in plain Java. A `RedriveTool` inspects each dead letter entry, classifies it as replayable or discardable, republishes replayable ones to a reprocessing topic, and the `IdempotentSettlementConsumer` applies each transfer at most once by remembering applied ids. The demo redrives a mix: a now-fixable transfer, a malformed one to discard, and a duplicate of an already-applied one. The code will show: a `DeadLetterEntry`, a `RedriveDecision`, the `RedriveTool`, the `IdempotentSettlementConsumer`, and a demo.

sections.s5_journey:
Input data: three dead letter entries — TRD-001 a now-fixable large transfer, TRD-002 a transient failure that was already partially applied, and TRD-BAD a malformed record.

Step 1: The operator confirms the bug that falsely rejected large transfers is fixed and deployed, which is the precondition for redrive.

Step 2: The redrive tool inspects TRD-001, sees it is not malformed, and classifies it REPLAY. It republishes it to the reprocessing path, the idempotent consumer has not seen TRD-001 before, so it settles it once and records the id.

Step 3: The tool inspects TRD-002, classifies it REPLAY, and republishes it. But the idempotent consumer already marked TRD-002 as applied from an earlier partial processing, so it recognizes the id and skips it, preventing a double settlement.

Step 4: The tool inspects TRD-BAD, sees it is malformed, and classifies it DISCARD. It is not replayed, because pushing it back would just re-poison the main flow. An audit entry records the discard.

Step 5: At the end, one record was newly settled, one was safely skipped as a duplicate, and one was discarded, so the dead letter queue was drained correctly without any double side effects and without re-poisoning the pipeline.

```
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [INFO   ] Inspect TRD-001 -> REPLAY (fix deployed, now processable)
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [INFO   ] Settled on replay: TRD-001 500000
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [INFO   ] Inspect TRD-002 -> REPLAY (fix deployed, now processable)
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [WARNING] Skip TRD-002 (already applied) — idempotent, no double settle
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [WARNING] Inspect TRD-BAD -> DISCARD (malformed, would re-poison)
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [INFO   ] Redrive complete: replayed=2, discarded=1
2026-10-24 20:50:21 [INFO   ] Consumer result: applied=1, skipped(duplicate)=1
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  PRECONDITION: bug fixed + deployed
    │
    ▼
  transfers.DLT ──inspect each entry──┐
    │                                  ▼
    │                            classify
    │                            ├─ malformed ───→ DISCARD (+ audit, do NOT replay)
    │                            └─ processable ─→ REPLAY
    │                                               │ throttled
    │                                               ▼
    │                                       transfers.reprocess
    │                                               │
    │                                               ▼
    │                            IdempotentSettlementConsumer
    │                               ├─ unseen id ──→ settle once
    │                               └─ seen id ────→ SKIP (no double settle)
    ▼
  Result: DLT drained, no duplicates, main topic not re-poisoned
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Redrive is the controlled process of moving records out of the dead letter queue back into the main flow so the now-fixed consumer can handle them, and the word controlled is the whole point. The absolute precondition is that the root-cause bug is fixed and deployed, because replaying before the fix just sends the records straight back to the dead letter queue. The dead letter records carry the metadata I captured when they failed, like the original topic, offset, exception, and a correlation id, which is what makes targeted reprocessing possible.

A safe redrive has three capabilities. First, inspection: I read the dead letter topic and examine each record and its error so I can tell a transient failure the fix now resolves from a permanent failure that should be corrected or discarded. Second, selective replay: for the records that should go back, I republish them, preserving the original key, usually to a dedicated reprocessing topic rather than straight onto the live main topic, so replayed traffic is isolated and I can throttle it to avoid overwhelming the consumers or downstream dependencies. Third, discard: genuinely unprocessable records are binned with an audit trail instead of being replayed.

The safety pillar is idempotent consumers. A record may have partially processed before it failed, or may be replayed more than once, so the consumer must produce the same result whether it sees a record once or many times, which I achieve by keying side effects on a business id, such as a unique constraint on the trade id, so a replay of an already-applied transfer is recognized and skipped. Without this, redrive risks double debits or double fees, which is unacceptable in a bank. The anti-pattern I never allow is blindly looping the whole dead letter queue back into the main topic, because any record that is still poisonous immediately re-fails and can stall or flood the pipeline, re-poisoning it.

In my banking platform at National Bank of India, a bug once falsely rejected large transfers and sent them to transfers.DLT. After we fixed and deployed the correction, we ran an audited, rate-limited redrive tool that inspected each record, replayed the processable ones to a separate reprocessing topic with the original key, and discarded the genuinely malformed ones. Because our settlement consumer is idempotent on the trade id, a transfer that had been partially applied before failing was recognized on replay and skipped rather than double-settled. The senior framing I give is that redrive is an explicit, observable, reversible operator action built on idempotent consumers and careful classification, not an automatic retry loop, and that is exactly what keeps a dead letter queue from becoming either a graveyard or a re-poisoning cannon.

---

keyPoints: Dead Letter Topic (DLT): store failed messages for later analysis
Retry topic: automatic retry with backoff before DLT
Poison pill: message that always fails — skip or DLT
